currentContext.expansion: FY26 expansion was retail-footprint led, not plant led. More than 180 new stores were added during the year, resulting in nearly 600,000 sq. ft. (nearly 0.6 million sq ft) of net retail space addition, with expansion momentum accelerating across priority markets; the Chairman's Message states the network now comprises 1,273 stores spanning over 7.9 million square feet, complemented by brand websites and leading digital marketplaces. New formats were launched - Galeries Lafayette (luxury) and OWND (value fashion, re-branded from Style Up); OWND alone added 34 stores while emphasis was also placed on optimizing its operating model, elevating merchandise architecture and building a scalable platform. TASVA strengthened its position in premium wedding wear through strategic expansion across key markets; Jaypore continued selective store expansion with stronger omni-channel capabilities; TCNS is in a transformation journey refreshing retail identity. E-commerce sales including TMRW grew more than 20% year-on-year to around 16% of revenue. The Company states it is investing in technology, retail expansion and future growth platforms. The fixed-asset footprint disclosed in BRSR Section A is 2 Factories, 3 Sampling Units and 6 Warehouses plus 7 named offices in India (row total printed as 18), with international plants and offices printed as a dash = stated NIL. STATED ABSENCE worth noting: BRSR Principle 2 Q1 reports R&D = 0 and Capex = 0 as a percentage of total R&D/capex invested in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, for BOTH FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, with the 'Details of improvements' column reading 'NA' (i.e. zero is stated, the explanation is unknown). DEMERGER FLAG: the AR mixes pre- and post-demerger material - Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited and Aditya Birla Garments Limited appear as parties under common control with effect from March 27, 2025, a business-overview banner is printed as 'ADITYA BIRLA FASHION AND APPAREL LIMITED - BUSINESS OVERVIEW' (a name that is not the reporting entity), and brand captions for Peter England and Hackett appear in the spread; comparatives are recorded as printed and are not reconciled here. currentContext.mdna: For consumer-facing sectors such as fashion retail the underlying environment remains constructive; demand may remain uneven in the near term but the medium-term consumption outlook remains structurally positive.|Indian apparel retail market estimated at around Rs 10 lakh crore in FY2025-26, projected to exceed Rs 14 lakh crore by FY2029-30 at a 9% CAGR, driven by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, deeper branded-apparel penetration and organised retail expanding into Tier-II and Tier-III cities.|Organised retail currently accounts for approximately 41% of India's apparel market and is expected to outpace the overall category, supported by brand-led formats, stronger retail infrastructure, international brand entry, digital commerce and omnichannel capabilities.|Global apparel market estimated at USD 1.84 trillion in calendar 2025, expected to reach around USD 1.9 trillion in 2026 (approximately 3.3% growth) and USD 2.54 trillion by 2033 at a 4.1% CAGR for 2026-2033; Asia Pacific was 40.8% of global apparel revenue in 2025.|Category growth rates stated: the organised value fashion market is growing at more than 15%; the occasion wear (ethnic) segment is growing at over 11%; D2C fashion brands continue to outpace the broader e-commerce fashion market.|Rising affluence - households in the Elite and Upper-Mid income cohorts growing 2X over 2019-30 versus less than 1X for lower cohorts (BCG X RAI 2022 chart), broadening the addressable market across premium, aspirational and value segments.|Indian macro: real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% for FY2025-26 with the RBI's FY2026-27 projection of 6.6%; growth broad-based, led by private consumption and investment, supported by personal tax relief, GST-related changes and continued formalisation.|Global macro: growth of around 3.4% in 2025, projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 - continuity in the economic cycle rather than a sharp break, with inflation and geopolitical risk as watchpoints.|Key near-term risk flagged: the West Asia conflict, through higher energy prices, freight costs and supply-chain disruptions, which could raise input costs and weigh on inflation and consumer sentiment.|Structural sector shifts management expects to drive the business: transition from unorganized to branded retail (most pronounced in Tier-II/Tier-III cities), omni-channel integration, next-gen (Gen Z and millennial) fashion consumption, hyper-personalised customer engagement, faster fashion cycles and speed-to-market, quick commerce and faster fulfilment, sustainability/ESG as a differentiator, and data-led decision making and AI adoption.|Recovery signals in India: early signs of recovery with consumers prioritising affordability, variety and price-value; festive and wedding-led demand, improving sentiment and traction in value and mass-premium formats have helped category momentum turn a corner.

risks.note: Global economic uncertainty, inflationary pressures, elevated household indebtedness and fluctuations in consumer sentiment may impact discretionary spending; prolonged demand softness could affect sales growth, profitability and inventory productivity. Mitigation stated: presence across multiple consumer segments, categories and price points, disciplined cost management, agile planning, stronger inventory and working-capital management, sourcing flexibility and channel-mix optimisation. Structural concentration reinforcing this risk: exports are only 1.04% of total turnover and the sole international market named is the USA, so essentially all demand is Indian discretionary consumption (BRSR Section A, back-filled from the registry/governance bundles). The MD&A separately flags the West Asia conflict as the key near-term risk, through higher energy prices, freight costs and supply-chain disruptions.

Rapidly changing consumer preferences, evolving lifestyles and increasing digital influence continue to reshape fashion consumption; failure to anticipate these shifts could impact product relevance, customer engagement and market share. Mitigation: continuous investment in consumer insights, product innovation, category expansion and digital capabilities, and a balanced portfolio across consumer segments and occasions.

Increasing use of digital platforms, interconnected systems and consumer data heightens exposure to cybersecurity threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; a significant incident could impact business continuity, stakeholder trust and brand reputation. Mitigation: cybersecurity and resilience framework with security controls, continuous monitoring, disaster recovery and business continuity, employee awareness programmes, vulnerability assessments and governance reviews; information and cyber security systems were independently assessed by one of the Big 4 audit firms.

Increasing competition for premium retail locations may constrain access to high-quality spaces and result in higher occupancy costs, affecting expansion plans, store economics and profitability - directly material given 1,273 stores over 7.9 million sq ft and continued footprint addition. Mitigation: market presence and long-standing developer/landlord relationships, plus focus on store productivity, space utilisation and in-store experience to maximise returns.

risks.risk: Talent attraction, retention and capability development
risks.note: Scaling across multiple verticals - design, retail, marketing, e-commerce and more - increases the need for skilled talent in a competitive Indian fashion retail sector. Mitigation: leadership development, succession planning, capability building, employee engagement, a strong employee value proposition, internal mobility, and access to the Aditya Birla Group's consumer-segment talent pool.

The Indian fashion and lifestyle market is highly competitive across organised and unorganised domestic players, international brands, digital-first businesses and emerging D2C brands; increased competition may lead to pricing pressure, higher customer acquisition costs and market-share erosion. Mitigation: brand equity, product innovation, wider consumer reach, differentiated cross-channel experiences, a diversified portfolio and omni-channel presence.

Reliance on digital platforms, automation, analytics and artificial intelligence brings risks of technology obsolescence, integration complexity, implementation challenges and evolving regulatory expectations; failure to adopt emerging technologies may impact operational efficiency and competitiveness. Mitigation: scalable platforms, phased implementation, strong governance, and continued investment in digital capability, data quality, process integration and responsible AI adoption.

The growth strategy involves scaling multiple businesses, expanding the retail footprint, strengthening omni-channel capabilities, integrating new platforms and driving operational transformation; delays in execution, ineffective implementation of strategic initiatives or inability to realise expected benefits may impact growth, profitability and return on investment. themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- For consumer-facing sectors such as fashion retail the underlying environment remains constructive; demand may remain uneven in the near term but the medium-term consumption outlook remains structurally positive.
- Indian apparel retail market estimated at around Rs 10 lakh crore in FY2025-26, projected to exceed Rs 14 lakh crore by FY2029-30 at a 9% CAGR, driven by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, deeper branded-apparel penetration and organised retail expanding into Tier-II and Tier-III cities.
- Organised retail currently accounts for approximately 41% of India's apparel market and is expected to outpace the overall category, supported by brand-led formats, stronger retail infrastructure, international brand entry, digital commerce and omnichannel capabilities.
- Global apparel market estimated at USD 1.84 trillion in calendar 2025, expected to reach around USD 1.9 trillion in 2026 (approximately 3.3% growth) and USD 2.54 trillion by 2033 at a 4.1% CAGR for 2026-2033; Asia Pacific was 40.8% of global apparel revenue in 2025.
- Category growth rates stated: the organised value fashion market is growing at more than 15%; the occasion wear (ethnic) segment is growing at over 11%; D2C fashion brands continue to outpace the broader e-commerce fashion market.
- Rising affluence - households in the Elite and Upper-Mid income cohorts growing 2X over 2019-30 versus less than 1X for lower cohorts (BCG X RAI 2022 chart), broadening the addressable market across premium, aspirational and value segments.
- Indian macro: real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% for FY2025-26 with the RBI's FY2026-27 projection of 6.6%; growth broad-based, led by private consumption and investment, supported by personal tax relief, GST-related changes and continued formalisation.
- Global macro: growth of around 3.4% in 2025, projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 - continuity in the economic cycle rather than a sharp break, with inflation and geopolitical risk as watchpoints.
- Key near-term risk flagged: the West Asia conflict, through higher energy prices, freight costs and supply-chain disruptions, which could raise input costs and weigh on inflation and consumer sentiment.
- Structural sector shifts management expects to drive the business: transition from unorganized to branded retail (most pronounced in Tier-II/Tier-III cities), omni-channel integration, next-gen (Gen Z and millennial) fashion consumption, hyper-personalised customer engagement, faster fashion cycles and speed-to-market, quick commerce and faster fulfilment, sustainability/ESG as a differentiator, and data-led decision making and AI adoption.
- Recovery signals in India: early signs of recovery with consumers prioritising affordability, variety and price-value; festive and wedding-led demand, improving sentiment and traction in value and mass-premium formats have helped category momentum turn a corner.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 expansion was retail-footprint led, not plant led. More than 180 new stores were added during the year, resulting in nearly 600,000 sq. ft. (nearly 0.6 million sq ft) of net retail space addition, with expansion momentum accelerating across priority markets; the Chairman's Message states the network now comprises 1,273 stores spanning over 7.9 million square feet, complemented by brand websites and leading digital marketplaces. New formats were launched - Galeries Lafayette (luxury) and OWND (value fashion, re-branded from Style Up); OWND alone added 34 stores while emphasis was also placed on optimizing its operating model, elevating merchandise architecture and building a scalable platform. TASVA strengthened its position in premium wedding wear through strategic expansion across key markets; Jaypore continued selective store expansion with stronger omni-channel capabilities; TCNS is in a transformation journey refreshing retail identity. E-commerce sales including TMRW grew more than 20% year-on-year to around 16% of revenue. The Company states it is investing in technology, retail expansion and future growth platforms. The fixed-asset footprint disclosed in BRSR Section A is 2 Factories, 3 Sampling Units and 6 Warehouses plus 7 named offices in India (row total printed as 18), with international plants and offices printed as a dash = stated NIL. STATED ABSENCE worth noting: BRSR Principle 2 Q1 reports R&D = 0 and Capex = 0 as a percentage of total R&D/capex invested in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, for BOTH FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, with the 'Details of improvements' column reading 'NA' (i.e. zero is stated, the explanation is unknown). DEMERGER FLAG: the AR mixes pre- and post-demerger material - Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited and Aditya Birla Garments Limited appear as parties under common control with effect from March 27, 2025, a business-overview banner is printed as 'ADITYA BIRLA FASHION AND APPAREL LIMITED - BUSINESS OVERVIEW' (a name that is not the reporting entity), and brand captions for Peter England and Hackett appear in the spread; comparatives are recorded as printed and are not reconciled here. NAMED DISCLOSURE DEFECTS (why capex_disclosed is empty): (1) '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE - CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' [page 218] prints header fragments 'FOR THE YEAR ENDED MARCH 31, 2026 | Year ended | As at | As at March 31, 2026', unit '` in Crore', row 'Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (net of advances)' followed by TWO figures, 32.89 and 61.20, with only ONE readable column date - the year-to-figure mapping cannot be read off the block, so neither figure is emitted rather than guessed. (2) '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE - SEGMENT CAPITAL EXPENDITURE ===' [page 297] header 'FOR THE YEAR ENDED MARCH 31, 2026 | As at | Year ended March 31, 2026 and as at March 31, 2026', row 'Capital expenditure' followed by five dashes (stated nil), and [page 298] header 'FOR THE YEAR ENDED MARCH 31, 2026 | Year ended March 31, 2025 and as at March 31, 2025 | Year ended | As at', row 'Capital expenditure' followed by 299.91, 187.37, 819.83, 1,307.11, -, 1,307.11. Neither block prints the segment column labels or a unit of measure, and a FY26 segment capex of all-nil is internally implausible against 180 new stores and 600,000 sq ft of net space added in the same year - so these figures are reported verbatim here and not emitted as data.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Multi-vertical portfolio architecture that lets the Company participate across price points, occasions, geographies and shopping behaviours - stated as the largest ethnic wear portfolio, a leading luxury retail platform, a dominant masstige and value retail presence and one of the largest digital-first brand portfolios
- One of India's largest fashion retail networks - 1,273 stores spanning over 7.9 million square feet, complemented by brand websites and leading digital marketplaces (Chairman's Message)
- India's largest and most comprehensive ethnic wear platform, addressing luxury couture, designer fashion, premium occasion wear and branded ethnic apparel
- Designer-led brand equity - Sabyasachi, Shantnu & Nikhil, Tarun Tahiliani and House of Masaba, with signature design language, craftsmanship and cultural relevance creating desirability across domestic and international markets
- Omni-channel capability with e-commerce revenue growing more than 20% year-on-year and contributing approximately 16% of total revenue
- Aditya Birla Group parentage - stated as a talent advantage giving access to a diverse and experienced consumer-segment talent pool, and a governance framework anchored in the Group Code of Conduct
- Long-standing relationships with developers and landlords used to secure strategic retail locations in a market where competition for premium retail space is rising
- TMRW Centre of Excellence (COE) enabling the digital-first brand portfolio of category leaders and category creators
- In-house manufacturing alongside retail (26.35% of turnover from manufacturing, 73.65% from retail trading) plus 3 sampling units supporting speed-to-market

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Ethnic — TCNS drag] The deck gives two readings of ethnic growth side by side: "Ethnic grew 4% vs LY" and "Ex. TCNS growth at 14%", indicating TCNS is materially diluting the reported ethnic number.
- [Cost inflation] Input cost pressures are flagged as emerging, with "inflation visible across raw materials, logistics and wages" and "further escalation remains a key monitorable".
- [Demand disruption] Occasion-led demand moderated YoY because "Adhik Maas disrupted the peak wedding related consumption this quarter", while broader demand was in line with previous quarters.
- [Channel shift] Quick commerce is called out as "emerging as a new growth channel" in the market update.
- [Definition] The deck defines secondary revenue as "the amount paid by consumer net of taxes" — the digital portfolio's 16% secondary revenue growth is on that basis, not reported revenue, and both that figure and the 11% portfolio revenue growth exclude WROGN.
